# Introduction

The [Allen Brain Cell (ABC) Atlas][abc-atlas] publishes single-cell,
single-nucleus and spatial transcriptomics data for the mouse and human
brain, including the whole mouse brain atlases of Yao et al. [-@yao2023]
and Zhang et al. [-@zhang2023]. The Allen Institute distributes these data
through a public cloud bucket together with a Python package,
`abc_atlas_access`, for discovering and downloading files.

`r Biocpkg("ABCatlas")` provides the same access directly in R, with no Python
installation. It goes further than downloading files: it assembles validated
cell and gene metadata for each curated dataset, selects cells, reports the
size of a request before transferring anything, and reads only the selected
cells and genes into Bioconductor objects such as
`r Biocpkg("SingleCellExperiment")` and `r Biocpkg("SpatialExperiment")`, or
into a Monocle 2 `CellDataSet` from `r Biocpkg("monocle")`.

The package separates metadata discovery and cell selection from expression
transfer:

1. `list_datasets()` discovers curated dataset routes.
2. `load_data()` assembles metadata and selects cells.
3. `plan_fetch()` previews the expression request and required files.
4. `fetch_data()` reads selected expression into the requested
R representation.

[abc-atlas]: https://portal.brain-map.org/atlases-and-data/bkp/abc-atlas

# Installation

Install the package from Bioconductor:

```{r install, eval=FALSE}
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages("BiocManager")
}
BiocManager::install("ABCatlas")
```

Then load it:

```{r library}
library(ABCatlas)
```

`ABCatlas` needs no Python, compiler or system libraries: HDF5 support comes
from `r Biocpkg("rhdf5")` and `r Biocpkg("Rhdf5lib")`, which bundle the HDF5
library on all platforms. Monocle 2 output additionally needs
`r Biocpkg("monocle")`, which is not installed with `ABCatlas` because of its
many dependencies; install it with `BiocManager::install("monocle")` when
needed. `ABCatlas` does need:

- **internet access** to the public ABC Atlas bucket
(`https://allen-brain-cell-atlas.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com`) the first
time each file is used. No account is needed. Behind a proxy, set the
`https_proxy` environment variable before starting R;
- **disk space** for the local cache (see Section
\@ref(cache-location-and-releases)).

# Discovering datasets

Use `list_datasets()` to inspect the curated routes supported by the package:

```{r list-datasets}
datasets <- list_datasets()
datasets
```

The catalog reports each route's modality, spatial and imputed status, default
representation and available expression representations. It is an ordinary
data frame:

```{r spatial-datasets}
datasets[datasets$spatial, ]
```

`list_datasets()` reads the package registry only and performs no network
access.

# Cache location and releases

ABC Atlas files are downloaded once and reused from a local cache. The cache
directory is resolved in this order:

1. explicit `download_base`;
2. `options(ABCatlas.download_base = ...)`;
3. the `ABC_ATLAS_CACHE` environment variable;
4. a per-user package cache directory.

This vignette caches files in a temporary directory:

```{r cache-dir}
cache_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "abc_atlas")
options(ABCatlas.download_base = cache_dir)
abc_download_dir()
```

In your own analyses, point the cache at a disk with enough free space; files
are then reused across R sessions. Metadata files are small, but a single
dataset's expression files can take several gigabytes. Only the files a
request needs are downloaded, and interrupted downloads resume where they
stopped.

The package is release-aware. Each function uses the ABC Atlas release
validated against this version of the package unless another `release` is
given, so analyses can be pinned to a release for reproducibility.

# Loading metadata

This vignette uses `Zhuang4`, a MERFISH spatial transcriptomics dataset from
Zhang et al. [-@zhang2023]. It is one of the smallest datasets in the atlas:
its metadata take about 40 MB and its expression files about 60 MB, so the
vignette downloads them when it is built.

`load_data()` downloads and assembles cell and gene metadata. It does not
fetch the expression matrices.

```{r load-data, message=FALSE}
abc <- load_data("Zhuang4")
abc
```

The result is an `abc_data` object containing cell metadata, gene metadata
and the unique values of the main metadata columns:

```{r inspect-metadata}
dim(abc$cell_metadata)
head(abc$cell_metadata[, c(
    "cell_label", "brain_section_label",
    "neurotransmitter", "class", "x", "y"
)])
head(abc$gene_data[, c("gene_identifier", "gene_symbol")])
abc$unique_values$neurotransmitter
```

It also retains dataset, cache and release provenance, so the object can be
passed directly to `plan_fetch()` and `fetch_data()`.

# Selecting cells

Selection happens during `load_data()`. Once files are cached, `load_data()`
reads them from the cache without downloading them again.

## Metadata filters

`filters` is a named list in which each name is a metadata column and each
value specifies which cells to retain:

```{r filter-cells, message=FALSE}
glut <- load_data(
    "Zhuang4",
    filters = list(neurotransmitter = "Glut")
)
nrow(glut$cell_metadata)
```

Multiple filters are combined: selected cells must satisfy every supplied
metadata condition.

## Exact cell identifiers

Use `cell_ids` when an exact set of cells is already known:

```{r select-cell-ids, message=FALSE}
my_cell_labels <- abc$cell_metadata$cell_label[1:5]

few <- load_data(
    "Zhuang4",
    cell_ids = my_cell_labels
)
few$cell_metadata$cell_label
```

Requested order is preserved. Duplicate identifiers and identifiers absent
after filtering are errors rather than silently altered selections.

## Reproducible sampling

Use `n_cells` to sample after filtering and exact-cell selection. The rest of
this vignette uses 500 glutamatergic cells:

```{r sample-cells, message=FALSE}
abc <- load_data(
    "Zhuang4",
    filters = list(neurotransmitter = "Glut"),
    n_cells = 500,
    seed = 1
)
abc
```

Sampling is reproducible for a fixed `seed`.

# Planning expression access

Expression files can be several gigabytes. Before downloading them, inspect
the request with `plan_fetch()`:

```{r plan-fetch}
genes <- c("Slc17a7", "Slc17a6", "Gad2", "Aqp4")

plan <- plan_fetch(abc, genes = genes, confirm = FALSE)
plan
```

A fetch plan reports the resolved release, the published representation
(`raw` or `log2`), the requested genes and cells, the expression files
involved, their sizes, whether each is cached, resumable partial bytes, the
additional download required and whether there is enough free disk space.
`plan_fetch()` does not download expression matrices.

In an interactive session, `plan_fetch()` prints the plan and asks whether to
proceed. An approved plan can then be passed to `fetch_data(plan = plan)`,
which downloads and reads exactly what was planned without asking again. This
vignette is built non-interactively, so it uses `confirm = FALSE` and the plan
is left unapproved:

```{r plan-approved}
plan$approved
```

# Fetching expression

`fetch_data()` downloads the expression files a request needs, then reads only
the selected cells and genes. Four output representations are available.

## Sparse matrix bundle

Called with an `abc_data` object and `genes`, `fetch_data()` downloads what is
needed directly:

```{r fetch-matrix, message=FALSE}
x <- fetch_data(
    abc,
    genes = genes,
    return_type = "matrix"
)

x$expression[, 1:5]
x$provenance
```

This returns an `abc_matrix` object containing sparse expression, selected
cell and gene metadata, and provenance, without requiring an
analysis-framework package.

The expression file is now cached, so a new plan for the same request needs no
download and is approved automatically. The remaining examples reuse it:

```{r plan-cached}
plan <- plan_fetch(abc, genes = genes, confirm = FALSE)
plan$total_download
plan$approved
```

## SingleCellExperiment

```{r fetch-sce, message=FALSE}
sce <- fetch_data(plan = plan, return_type = "sce")
sce
```

Raw expression uses a `counts` assay; upstream transformed expression uses a
`log2` assay. Provenance is stored in the object metadata:

```{r sce-provenance}
S4Vectors::metadata(sce)$ABCatlas$release
```

## SpatialExperiment

`Zhuang4` is declared a spatial route, so its spatial coordinates are attached
automatically:

```{r fetch-spatial, message=FALSE}
spe <- fetch_data(plan = plan, return_type = "spatial")
spe

head(SpatialExperiment::spatialCoords(spe))
```

Automatic coordinate inference is restricted to routes declared spatial. For
metadata from other routes, verified coordinate columns must be supplied
explicitly with `coordinate_columns`. This guard prevents
dimensionality-reduction coordinates from being misrepresented as physical
spatial locations:

```{r fetch-spatial-coordinates, eval=FALSE}
x <- fetch_data(
    other_abc,
    genes = genes,
    return_type = "spatial",
    coordinate_columns = c("x_experiment", "y_experiment")
)
```

## Monocle 2

```{r fetch-monocle, message=FALSE}
cds <- fetch_data(plan = plan, return_type = "monocle")
cds
```

Monocle 2 output requires the `r Biocpkg("monocle")` package and is returned
as a `CellDataSet` using the published raw
expression representation. Published `log2` expression is not converted into
count semantics for Monocle 2. Provenance is stored in
`Biobase::experimentData(cds)@other$ABCatlas`.

# Raw, log2 and imputed expression

Expression representations are properties of the published dataset route, not
transformations performed by `ABCatlas`:

```{r data-types}
as.data.frame(list_datasets())[
    ,
    c(
        "dataset",
        "default_data_type",
        "available_data_types",
        "imputed"
    )
]
```

`data_type = "raw"` retains count semantics. `data_type = "log2"` returns the
upstream published transformed values; the package does not reinterpret them
as counts.

`MERFISH_imputed` is a separate route for upstream published imputed spatial
expression. `ABCatlas` does not perform imputation. Its default and available
representation is `log2`.

# Gene identifiers and symbols

Expression rows are keyed by canonical `gene_identifier`:

```{r inspect-genes}
SummarizedExperiment::rowData(sce)[, c("gene_identifier", "gene_symbol")]
```

Gene symbols can be supplied to `genes` when they resolve uniquely. If a
symbol maps to several features, the package reports the ambiguity and asks
for a canonical identifier rather than silently selecting one. The package
ships a tiny offline example release in which the symbol `Aaa` maps to two
features:

```{r ambiguous-symbol, error=TRUE}
example_dir <- system.file("extdata", "ex", package = "ABCatlas")
example_data <- readRDS(file.path(example_dir, "example-data.rds"))
example_data$genes

fetch_data(
    download_base = example_dir,
    metadata = example_data$cells,
    gene_data = example_data$genes,
    genes = "Aaa",
    return_type = "matrix",
    offline = TRUE,
    release = "20250101"
)
```

For source datasets containing duplicate published feature identifiers,
distinct canonical feature identities are preserved instead of inventing
symbol-based identities.

# Offline use

Once the required files are cached, `offline = TRUE` prevents network access.
Everything this vignette needs is now cached, so this runs without the
network:

```{r offline-workflow, message=FALSE}
abc_offline <- load_data(
    "Zhuang4",
    filters = list(neurotransmitter = "Glut"),
    n_cells = 500,
    seed = 1,
    offline = TRUE
)

x <- fetch_data(
    abc_offline,
    genes = genes,
    return_type = "matrix",
    offline = TRUE
)
dim(x$expression)
```

In offline mode, missing files are errors rather than triggering downloads.

# Direct cache access

`abc_cache_connect()` provides lower-level access to files in the release
manifest:

```{r cache-metadata}
cache <- abc_cache_connect()
cache

gene_table <- cache$get_metadata_dataframe(
    directory = "Zhuang-ABCA-4",
    file_name = "gene"
)
dim(gene_table)
```

`cache$get_file_path()` returns a local path, downloading the requested file
when necessary unless the cache is offline.

# Working with larger datasets

Other datasets use exactly the same functions. They are not run here because
of their size. For example, the Aging Mouse dataset's metadata take about
700 MB and its expression is a single file of about 13 GB:

```{r aging-mouse, eval=FALSE}
abc <- load_data(
    "AgingMouse",
    filters = list(anatomical_division_label = "STR"),
    n_cells = 1000,
    seed = 1
)

genes <- c("P2ry12", "Cx3cr1", "Tmem119")

# Interactively, this prints the plan and asks before downloading
plan <- plan_fetch(abc, genes = genes)

sce <- fetch_data(plan = plan, return_type = "sce")
```

Run `plan_fetch()` before `fetch_data()` on large datasets to see how much
will be downloaded and whether there is enough disk space.
